trial_court: Senior Civil Judge, Repalle (OS No.6 of 2011) and Additional District and Sessions Judge, Tenali (A.S.No.34 of 2015)
case_name: Kothapalli Venakteswara Rao vs Myneni Raghavamma 2 Others

parties.respondent_defendant: Myneni Raghavamma, Katragadda Radha Bai, Myneni Bala Koteswara Rao (Respondents/Plaintiffs)

facts_of_case: Suit filed for partition, court decreed property to be divided into 12 equal shares and separate possession of share to each of the plaintiffs.

legal_principles.principle: A gift deed reciting that the property is being gifted to a person as the properties given by her in laws are not sufficient for her maintenance does not enlarge into an absolute right.
legal_principles.held: The very small issue involved in this appeal is whether the property, which was given to Durgamma towards maintenance with limited rights, has enlarged into an absolute right by virtue of Section 14i) of the Hindu Succession Act or whether Kiurgamma would have only limited right over the suit schedule property without any right of alienation.

legal_principles.principle: A person who executes a Will in favour of another has no right to execute the Will if it is not valid and binding.
legal_principles.held: Durgamma has no right to execute the Will in favour of the mother of the defendant or to any other person.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's judgment and decree were confirmed by the additional district and sessions judge, Tenali.

use_for_drafting: representing legal heirs in succession matters
